cards.title: Government two-party preferred
cards.sub: Governing-party 2PP, with a historical fan chart for all previous terms since 1972
cards.insight: 16 months in, Labor (51.2% against One Nation) sits 1.9 points above the average government at this point.
cards.basis: Every line is the implied two-party figure: each poll’s primary votes read through the preferences counted at the election that opened its term – last-election flows.

cards.title: Government primary vote
cards.sub: First-preference support for the governing party, with a historical fan chart for all previous terms since 1972
cards.insight: 16 months in, Labor (26.8%) sits 14.5 points below the average government at this point. The second and third lowest at this point were Gillard (33.1%) and Albanese (33.8%).

cards.title: Opposition primary vote
cards.sub: First-preference support for the opposition party, with a historical fan chart for all previous terms since 1972
cards.insight: 16 months in, the Coalition (21.2%) sits 21.1 points below the average opposition at this point. The second and third lowest at this point were Albanese (32.5%) and Dutton (34.7%).

cards.title: Preferred prime minister
cards.sub: PM’s lead on the preferred-PM question, with a historical fan chart for all previous terms since 1984
cards.insight: 16 months in, Albanese (+12.0) sits 1.1 points below the average prime minister at this point.

cards.title: Prime minister net approval
cards.sub: Approval minus disapproval, with a historical fan chart for all previous terms since 1972
cards.insight: 16 months in, Albanese (−24.6) sits 25.3 points below the average prime minister at this point. Only Whitlam (1974, −25.5) sat lower at this point.

cards.title: Opposition leader net approval
cards.sub: Approval minus disapproval, with a historical fan chart for all previous terms since 1972
cards.insight: 16 months in, Taylor (−6.9) sits 2.5 points below the average opposition leader at this point.
